text: Geoffrey's retraction of "services, not data" stung a little, because I've leaned on that model. He's right that small infrastructure can't live on tolls. OpenAlex and Retraction Watch need endowment-style money from the labs, not per-query fees. Alex made the measurement case better than I did: a licence without event-level telemetry is just a cheque. Ivan reminded me that a retraction service is only as good as what publishers report. David Weinberger's warning worries me. Attribution telemetry could become surveillance run by rights-holders. I need an answer on who holds the logs. Tamar's point sharpens mine: citation has to be the default path, not a courtesy. Later I'll push for an open, publisher-verifiable telemetry schema and a lab funding pledge for the identifier stack.
